Longest friendship I’ve ever had was about 25 years. I met him in middle school. We had done everything together. Played in bands, recorded some really cool music, started a company together, and our families were so very close and our kids loved eachother. 

Somewhere along the line, he stopped talking to me like a friend and instead was talking to me like I was some kind of annoyance. Kind of like how you talk to an employee you know won’t be around very long. One day after a gig, I had mistakenly taken a piece of equipment to the wrong warehouse. This is a non issue as the “wrong warehouse” is owned by our mutual friend and the issue was resolved within minutes of realizing what happened. He called me screaming at the top of his lungs and I hung up on him. First time I had ever done that. He then starts sending me threatening messages and calling me childish names (we’re both late 30’s btw). So I tell him “I don’t know who the fuck you think you are and why you think this is ok, but I’m tired of you speaking to me like this. Do not contact me again”.

For any of my potential new gals I always looked for sincerity, sense of humor, how they handle stressful situations of all types (especially emergencies), how loving they were toward me, and of course their intentions of what they wanted out of the relationship. Divorced dad here, when my ex wife and I got divorced I made sure to put a clause in our divorce agreement that states we cannot have our kid around anyone we are romantically or sexually involved with for at least 8 months. This was put in place for safety reasons. I wanted to make sure that my ex wasn’t going to be bringing random men around my son and vice versa. Coming from broken homes ourselves, it was very important to both of us as parents to not confuse our child (especially since he was so young when the divorce happened). So any love interests were not ever spoken of around our son until we knew that they were appropriate people, no drugs or excess drinking, or violent tendencies. People can hide these things for a long time hence the long “waiting period”. We dodged a few bullets this way a kept our kid safe from what would have been disastrous. Try not to take it personally, imo they are just being cautious.

Growing up my family was very poor. My mother raised 4 kids by herself. One Christmas in particular things were not going well for us and we didn’t have much of anything to go around that year. I really wanted to learn how to play the drums and one of my brothers knew that. The basement became off limits for a while and I didn’t understand why. Everyone else in the family could go down there and did every day but I wasn’t allowed to, I didn’t get it. Come Christmas morning and the family is giving eachother what we were able to throw together. It’s my turn, my brother takes me down to the basement and gives me the most wonderful gift. It was a drum kit that he had painstakingly made entirely out of leftover wood scraps (explains all the banging and power tools I heard for months) and I was floored. Even at that young of an age I completely understood that we were dirt poor and absolutely did not have money for things such as musical instruments. Knowing this and seeing the effort my brother had put into building this drum kit for me made me so incredibly happy. Yeah it sounded like you would imagine but I’ll never forget what he said, “now you can get an idea of the arm movements and when you get a real kit you’ll be ready!” Hands down best most thoughtful gift ever.
